Precious Metals Quarterly 2011 Q3 # Executive summary ## Silver: Fundamental surplus to persist Silver’s fundamental surplus has narrowed and investor demand does not therefore have to be as strong for it to be the key driver in the market. Quotations will remain elevated so long as investors seek a safe haven and consider silver to be such an asset. We assume that silver’s price will remain supported until 2013 at which point we expect it to begin falling. - Fabrication demand in 2010 more than recovered what it lost in 2009 helped by burgeoning demand for silver coins. Growth in total fabrication demand will be limited beyond 2011 as major falls in demand for silver coins offset much of the growth in silver’s other uses. - Mine production is forecast to begin falling short of total potential in 2014 as silver’s falling price prompts the owners of many projects to defer commissioning indefinitely. - Excess silver supplies are forecast to run at a level no greater than 3,500 t/y through to 2016. This will leave stock levels about 34,000 tonnes high than they were in the mid-2000s. ### **Silver’s recent fall has left it $20/oz below its high for this year** 50 London silver fix; $/oz

CRU International Limited confidential 2 Precious Metals Quarterly 2011 Q3 Executive Summary ## Other precious metal markets #### Gold The downward trend in the gold market’s surplus is set to continue over the next five years, but the fundamental balance is not expected to shift into deficit at any point in our forecast period. - The world’s gold supplies were essentially unchanged in the first half of 2011 as a marginal rise in mine output was largely offset by declining flows of recycled metal. - Demand from industrial users, particularly jewellery, is expected to be lower over the forecast period since higher average annual gold prices are now expected for each year in our outlook. - Demand from central banks and investors, who see gold as a safe haven during times of global financial turmoil, remains strong and will keep providing support to gold prices. #### Platinum The magnitude of platinum oversupply will continue easing this year. The return of the market to a closer balance is then expected next year before the market switches to persistent deficit in 2013-16. - Our current outlook for platinum demand growth is lower than in June due to a larger than earlier expected drop in demand from glass and electronics producers. - Platinum mine supply has been revised lower to reflect a challenging industrial relations climate within the South African mining industry and increased political pressure on platinum miners operating in Zimbabwe. - If current worries over the world economy prove too ex

Should you have any problems with using the CRUOnline website, please contact the helpdesk on Tel +44 20 7903 2113 (09.00–18.00 UK time), or e-mail:- support.cruonline@crugroup.com The following lists the different statistics and downloads that are available to you as a _Precious Metals Quarterly_ subscriber: ##### **Quarterly Report** - Pdf version of this report - Separate excel workbooks with our forecast tables for gold, silver, platinum and - palladium (supply-demand balances, consumption by country and use, mine production by country and operation, scrap generation, more) ##### **Market Statistics** (all in excel) - COTF futures and options contracts - Gold, silver, platinum and palladium ETF holdings - Prices (precious metals prices and other key indicators) - Statistics (summarised data on prices, exchanges, exchange rates, local prices etc) - Gold, silver, platinum and palladium bullion imports by country - Central Bank gold reserves - UK jewellery hallmarkings - Bombay gold prices and premia - LBMA monthly clearing turnover statistics for gold and silver - Lease rates for gold and silver - US Eagle coin sales C

## Data sources and study team 

The historical data presented in this report are based on estimates published by a variety of sources, including Johnson Matthey (JM), World Gold Council (WGC), International Financial Statistics (IFS), JD Power, London Bullion Market Association (LBMA), World Bureau of Metal Statistics (WBMS), GTIS trade statistics, and company websites and written reports. 

However, CRU’s interpretation of these data may or may not coincide with those expressed in these various sources. 

The forecast is exclusively CRU’s.
